subject: Biochemistry & genetics
summary: Adenylate cyclase (AC) converts ATP to cyclic AMP, a key second messenger that regulates metabolism, hormone signaling, and ion transport. Clinicians must recognize how altered AC activity underlies diseases like cholera, heart failure, and certain endocrine tumors.

sections.p: A membrane‑bound enzyme that synthesizes cAMP from ATP when activated by G‑protein α‑subunits or forskolin. cAMP activates protein kinase A, altering cellular functions.
b: AC is activated by G‑s and inhibited by G‑i

sections.p: Binding of an activated G‑s α‑subunit to AC changes its conformation, allowing ATP to be cyclized to cAMP. cAMP then binds PKA regulatory subunits, releasing catalytic activity.
AC activity is increased by G‑s‑coupled receptors (β‑adrenergic, glucagon) and decreased by G‑i‑coupled receptors (α2‑adrenergic, muscarinic). Phosphodiesterases degrade cAMP, providing feedback.

Excessive AC activation (e.g., cholera toxin, β‑agonist overdose) causes high cAMP → secretory diarrhea or tachyarrhythmia. Loss of AC function can blunt hormonal responses, seen in some endocrine tumors.
b: Cholera toxin ADP‑ribosylates G‑s → constitutive AC

sections.p: Understanding AC helps manage conditions where cAMP is central: cholera diarrhea, heart failure (β‑blockers reduce AC drive), and certain endocrine neoplasms (e.g., McCune‑Albright syndrome).
b: β‑blockers ↓ AC activity in heart failure
cAMP‑driven tumors may respond to PKA inhibitors

t.b: Is ventricular function reduced due to chronic β‑adrenergic stimulation? Low EF supports AC‑mediated cardiomyopathy

sections.p: Focus on the link between G‑protein signaling, AC, cAMP, and downstream effects. Remember cholera toxin mechanism and why β‑blockers are used in heart failure.

whenToSeekHelp: Acute decompensated heart failure with pulmonary edema
Sudden tachyarrhythmia unresponsive to standard therapy

faq.a: Cholera toxin ADP‑ribosylates G‑s, locking it active, so AC continuously makes cAMP, driving chloride and water secretion.

faq.q: Why are β‑blockers used in heart failure?
faq.a: They block β‑adrenergic receptors, reducing G‑s activation of AC, lowering cAMP and myocardial oxygen demand.

faq.q: What test confirms excess cAMP activity?
faq.a: Direct cAMP measurement is rarely available; clinical clues (e.g., cholera stool studies, hormone assays) are used instead.

exam: Explain the mechanism by which cholera toxin increases intestinal secretion.
Describe how β‑adrenergic antagonists improve outcomes in chronic heart failure.
Differentiate G‑s and G‑i effects on adenylate cyclase and downstream cAMP levels.
